utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...-- That you will not be here on Friday, because that is the reason we are not sitting on Friday, that you provide the Prosecution by today or agree with them by today what will be the calling order. I take it that if exhibits that were attached to letters have not been attached, that you provide the Prosecution with them as well. And could you please indicate also to the Defence [sic] which exhibits, which documents will be tendered through which witnesses, if that is not clear. You can discuss it during the break that follows. If there is any need -- I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is one intervention. I am waiting urgently to receive answers to things I have asked Mr. Ierace. I asked Mr. Ierace to reply to us in writing. We are waiting and waiting and waiting. And I would like to ask him if we could get a formal answer after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On what actually?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the break. Well we have asked questions, for instance, with regards to the witness addresses, we are still waiting for those answers. I have asked very strict, clear questions on the modus operandi with regards to the next people, with regards to the fact whether we could find some points of agreements. And I am still waiting for those answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we filed -- we went to the Registry this afternoon to comply with the 10-day requirement that you set in relation to agreed facts. We are told that that filing will be accepted on Friday, so my response is contained in that. I did write to the Defence I think a week ago, last Friday it was, with information as to the location of witnesses that the Defence proposes to call. I am unaware of any other outstanding matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When I said if there is any need, that is when you interrupted me, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if there would be any need for assistance during the meeting, during the break, as far as the calling order is concerned, then I will be available. We will have a break until 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...until five past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue to examine the witness, the Chamber received this morning an application for leave for appeal on a decision in respect of cooperation between the parties. I don't know whether you intended to respond to that motion, but the Chamber would like to receive that response as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It is in French, it is being translated. Would Monday afternoon be acceptable?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom again. And the parties can address the Registrar after this hearing in order to see how they can get the assistance that was offered to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it has been done already. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to seek the usher's help.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will show you a map and it could be used. This is a colour map. And it could be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the transcript it is the exhibit which has D1766. Thank you. Could you please focus it so that we can have a clearer image. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you recognise this as the map of a part of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And in this part of the map do you recognise the place where you were engaged as a soldier during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just point at it with the pointer which I believe have a pen there, and would you please point to it on the map. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is Aleja Lipa Street, now Djure Salaja, downstream the Miljacka River, downstream the Miljacka. This street Porodice Ribra -- no, no, no, sorry, just a moment, Djure Salaja to Strojorad and then we go straight up towards the stadium. And then at this stadium in this corner, there was a Serb position and then it went like this straight on. This is the police centre, police centre, police club. And then it went up again to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, I will stop you. Because we shall see it on a blownup map better. But now, can you tell us, for the whole, can you repeat for the area as such that we are talking about. The area that we can now see clearly on the screen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like this. I said, the street here which is called --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, wait. Sorry. Don't give us the street names right now. Only -- only quietly make a round -- make a circle around the area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand now, yes. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, for the witness -- no, sorry for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has made a line from the Miljacka River then going southward practically parallel to the blue line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we do not know where it starts. There are a lot of blue lines and south is available -- could we just try to -- the line indicated by the witness started approximately on the southern bank of the river, just left from where the word "Miljacka" appears would then go into westerly direction until the first blue grid line where it reads "STOJAD," would then go south and pass by the stadium Grbavica, mainly on the eastern side, would then go to an a structure indicated on the red in the map which is just south-easterly of the stadium, would then go further south up to a road, and would go in an easterly direction on a white road in the direction of number "633" on the map. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we need to be precise. It is not near number 633, but in the direction of 33. It very important and we shall see why in a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what the English transcript and what my words said. [Interpretation] That is what I said in the -- towards number 633. Exactly that is what I was pointing out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, might it be more helpful if the witness would actually draw this on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it would be preferable, but there are certain reasons why the Defence prefer the witness not to do this at this very moment, although it would have been more efficient. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is right, Mr. President, because he will do it on a different map, which is -- I am saying this in order to facilitate the process. The map 3728, we already have copies so that we can be prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you are talking to us about the rear. I am referring to your earlier answers. Would you please just point at -- with the tool that you have, the pointer, would you please point at the area that you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is indicating --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is indicating on the map the whole area behind, that is south of the Miljacka which ends after an intersection. Before well before number 633. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you can now take your pointer back. Thank you. In the area that you mentioned, do you know if there was any destruction of urban structure? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. How would you qualify the destruction, I mean in quantitative terms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My positions were almost daily hit by 10 to 15 mortar shells, my positions, not counting small arms ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you talk to us about your positions. Do you or can you have any knowledge of all of the projectiles intended for you, for your positions, reached their target?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Few of them hit the marker. Most of them hit civilian objects. There were a few of them which hit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And how do you explain that fact?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. This entire line of questioning calls for speculation. There is no basis or foundation that the witness has any knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we have had a similar situation before. You were then instructed how to proceed. Would you please do it in a similar way now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, during the conflict, did you have daily experience of shelling? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you take note, become aware of some cases of those shots of some errors, firing errors, do you have any knowledge about the possibility of firing errors and are you competent enough to know such things and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they -- and they must have known where our lines were, and I presumed they fired at our lines. But they were not doing it well was that it was mostly civilians who fell victim. Very few of their mortar shells hit our trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you about to tell us that the targets which were the trenches were relatively narrow and that therefore they were difficult to hit, according to your experience?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I withdraw it. I will rephrase my question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Do you have specific knowledge on the use of mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you fire mortars yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any training in firing mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know in the branch of the army that I served did not have any mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have knowledge on the precision of artillery weapons, the artillery that -- the precision that could be achieved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The precision is possible, but the shells are always charged the same, that is, they can fall 100 metres away, plus or minus, because they do not all carry the same charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This 100 metres, is that the difference in the charge that is used or is this something else you are referring to? You say 100 metres' difference. Could you explain this exactly what you meant.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An error is also possible. You see and I suppose they were firing at our trenches, but their shells would go off the mark and then affect innocent people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say, they fired at our trenches, but they missed and they hit innocent people. On the basis of what do you exactly conclude that they fired at your trenches and missed rather than that they, for example, intentionally targeted those innocent people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I believe that it is part of the military Code of Conduct, that you target military not the civilian. I cannot understand that there can be a human being who will fire at a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. civilian rather than at a soldier who could be deemed responsible for something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would there be any other reason for you to assume that your trenches were the targets and that the shells missed their targets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The separation lines between the Serb troops and the Bosniak troop at times were only 20 metres away. So perhaps somebody feared that he wouldn't reach the target and, therefore, fired and, therefore, targeted something that was at a greater distance, and that is how they hit civilians. That is one assumption that I make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you: Would that mean that intentionally not your positions were targeted because the other party would be afraid of firing errors and, therefore, for the risk to hit their own positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, that was probably how it was, along the lines which were nearby. And the lines which were further away, they -- shots were more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say if the confrontation lines were close, they were able to fire with great precision and would just fire a bit further than your lines because they wanted to avoid the risk of hitting their own positions. And where the confrontation lines were further away, there they made firing errors when they did not hit the confrontation line, and hit instead innocent people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, when they were further away, saying when men was not responsible, but the charge of the mortar -- shells, shells were frequently made during the war and therefore not charged properly, according to the regulations, and that is why sometimes they fell short of the target or went over the target. That is what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What makes you believe that this charging of the shells caused the firing errors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because technically speaking, every shell should have a particular gunpowder charge defined for a particular shell calibre. But those shells were not built in such a way. So that -- I mean, they were not calculated precisely or were not charged precisely, and therefore the trajectory would be either shorter or longer than envisaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What knowledge do you have on the production of shells used by the other party in the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I know more or less places where they could be doing that. But I am saying because they were made in the factory that I used to work, because that was a military factory. And that factory had all the possible mechanical assets to make the shells. And I also attended the mechanical schools at Marijin Dvor between the Holiday Inn Hotel and Marshal Tito Barracks. And that school was accommodated in the basement where they had a wonderful workshop where they could make all this. And I also received information from a friend who spent the whole war on the federal side. They were assembling them in the television building, in the Sarajevo television building at Alipasino Polje on the underground floor. And throughout the war, that is where they made those shells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you for your intervention. I am not sure that it is an interpretation error, but I think that the witness said "I also attended a mechanical school" and in the transcript in page 73, line 18, I think that the witness said that there were also some production units in the mechanical school. We can ask it perhaps once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned a mechanical school. Is it a place where weapons were manufactured to what you know? Will you please tell us aloud what your answer is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. That was clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...that the witness is invited to tell it aloud, and that is what he did. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, on the map that you have, that is the one which shows the -- is the section of Sarajevo, could you indicate certain workshops which made weapons which you said? Could you do that? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, Witness, I will ask that you be given a black marker. And I shall appreciate it if you put a cross at a place that you mentioned and that we can see on this map. Point by point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will stop you here. Could you please indicate next to the cross write a "1." You can maybe draw a larger cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. What are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the mechanical school in Marijin Dvor in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please show us a second place -- but just one second. Please wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the Prosecution would object and ask that this be clarified. Previously the witness testified as to a list -- of listed a number of places where he said shells could have been made. And the Defence is now asking the witness to mark places "were" made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please verify, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the source of the knowledge and perhaps also relate it in time because the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Of course. Very well, but I must say that I am just asking questions with regards to his knowledge, if he knew where these shells were built.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, Witness, could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that is not a solution to the problem. Because if you say "to your knowledge," that could be to your knowledge of where they could have been made or as to your knowledge as where they were made. So please try to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us: How did you find out about this, about these facts? How have you learned of this and so on and so forth? And, Witness, please do not mark anything on the map right now, for the time being. Just answer my question: How did you learn about these facts that you just mentioned a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have learned about this -- not only myself but also other members, other soldiers found out about this from the people who were living in the federal part of Sarajevo. This was also on my line hotel -- the hotel Bristol was also on my line and that was actually just across from my line there was a bridge. And under the bridge, the citizens who did not have enough money to pay to the teams that were proceeding to the exchanges, they had to leave at night through the Muslim positions or leave the Muslim positions --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is not clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, this is why, if we talk about Marijin Dvor, we had to go along Miljacka and that was held by the HVO. So these were not Muslim positions, but Croatian positions. And those Croats were very generous, so to speak, towards the citizens because they would let them go through their lines during the night. And they would exit on the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you to listen carefully to the question and specifically answer to that question. I think the question was about how you knew about this ammunition production. You did write a "1" on the map. Could you tell us precisely and answer the question of

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How you know that there was a production facility for mortars or ammunition? Let me say it a more general way. Did you see it yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We found out about this through the citizen who had left. So the war began in Sarajevo, these people left the city --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first question was: Did you see it yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was not able to see it myself because it was on the enemy side, on the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you didn't see it yourself, did you hear it from someone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the citizens that had seen it themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many citizens have told you this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Left by thousands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thousands of citizens have told you about the production facility there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the people who left confirmed this facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was: How many told you this? How many people told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, personally to myself, 20 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know their names or were they --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course I know. But for most of these people still live in the Federation, so I wouldn't really disclose their personal data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are solutions for that. If you would like to mention names and not this to be made known to the public, there are solutions for that. But, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I tried. The witness seems to give wide answers on questions. Could you please try to keep it in such a way that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I will do so. And Mr. President, what we could do is to ask to go into a closed session and ask the witness to give us some names, if this is a sufficient guarantee. I believe that it would, but of course, this is with your leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would like to find out about these names, then we should do that in closed session. So if you think it is relevant, we could go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we can do so and the witness may perhaps answer to this question and perhaps give us three names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. President, let me just check. Do we have some more time or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there would be one or two questions, to finish a certain subject, fine; if not, then I would like to finish now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you do this for us, please, very briefly. You have the map before you. Could you be kind enough to but some crosses corresponding to each of these production facilities, accompanied by numbers. Do not tell us what these are all about. And on Monday, we will talk about what they represent. So just draw the crosses and then we shall end your examination of today. So just put some crosses there. And write numbers two, three, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need another map because we cannot see the south-east part of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But there are no other sites that you could indicate to us on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was Hum, and then Zrak would be here, and the television station should be here. So we don't have those parts, they are missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. We can cover this during the next session. It would be probably wiser to do so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. We have to stop at a quarter to 7.00, Mr. DP10. Unfortunately, since we are not sitting on Thursday and Friday, exceptionally, we will continue only on next Monday and that would be in the morning at 9.00. So I hope to see you then again. You are ordered not to speak with anyone about the testimony you gave in this court. So that would be valid up until Monday. Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom. Although I do hesitate, if there is any specific issues that have to be dealt with by the parties that could wait until next Monday, I know that we are -- there is a couple of days. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, very quickly if I could. I note that this witness has been talking for the past 10 or 15 minutes about locations of mortar production or shell production facilities. And I do draw to the attention of the Chamber that this is not included in the expanded 65 Rule ter statement that we received from the Defence and perhaps if Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down, Mr. Mundis, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would not blame the Defence for that since it resulted from a question I put to the witness as to the production of mortars where I asked questions about precisions of mortars. So it's -- I cannot imagine that it would not have been expected by the Defence that this information would come up. On the other hand, if it is not specifically sought, of course, one could wonder how much attention we will pay to it on the whole. But I would in this case not blame the Defence for not having it put in its summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That was just a prefatory statement, Mr. President. I note that the expanded summary that we received with respect to this witness was faxed on the 13th of October. And perhaps in light of the Chamber's ruling, oral ruling, yesterday with respect to the specifics that should be in the Rule 65 ter, or the expanded 65 ter summaries, I do Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. note that this witness is -- the statement is -- his testimony is relevant for scheduled sniping incidents number 15 and 20. And perhaps during the course of the next couple of days prior to Monday, if we could be given any additional information that the Defence expects to lead from this witness, that would be greatly appreciated

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is sniping incidents 15 and 20 the Chamber instructed the Defence to give details, if there are any details, as to the relevance for his testimony on these two sniping incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I have a feeling that we will be in close contact with the Prosecution. If I am not mistaken, we are mainly talking about the incident number 10 if my memory serves me well, but I should verify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the summary, the last line of the summary is -- his testimony is relevant for scheduled sniping incidents number 15 and 20. Would you say that -- and that is language that differs a bit from what we find at the end of some other summaries, where it often says, he will speak about facts important for scheduled sniping incidents, et cetera, et cetera. So the language is different here. If there are specific facts apart from those already mentioned in the summary, that would be relevant for sniping incidents number 15 and 20, you should inform the Prosecution. If it is just that you indicated that these subjects as such bear some relevance for these scheduled sniping incidents, then of course there are no new facts to be expected to come up during the testimony. No other points? Could the Prosecution be informed not later than Friday about this. And assistance is offered as always. Is there any issue you would like to raise and which is really necessary to be raised until next Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I still -- I am still waiting for my answers, but I am used to it. I am getting used to it. So nothing more to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until next Monday morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
